blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Multi-instance partial-label learning (MIPL) addresses inexact supervision in both the instance and label spaces, which can be applied to video classification.
However, bag-level labels do not explicitly supervise the correspondence between candidate classes and temporal evidence. We propose PivotMipl , which couples label disambiguation with temporal evidence allocation through a joint class–time assignment. Occupancy-regularized spherical matching associates contextualized video features while learning nonuniform temporal mass and discouraging excessive concentration. During training, candidate-restricted inference recomputes the assignment within the candidate label set. A dual-marginal KL projection then constructs a structured teacher that incorporates momentum-refined class beliefs while preserving the proposal’s temporal occupancy. A single plan-level KL objective aligns the full-space predictor with this teacher. Our analysis characterizes when candidate re-solving differs from masking and shows that, under the stated construction, the joint objective decomposes into class-marginal and class-conditional temporal supervision. We construct VCMIPL benchmarks from Breakfast, DoTA, and FineAction using model-generated candidate labels and evaluate the method across four feature representations. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that PivotMipl outperforms existing MIPL algorithms in both effectiveness and efficiency.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Learning to classify videos from weak annotations requires identifying both the true label and its supporting temporal evidence. Video-level labels do not specify which frames or clips support the target class within a sequence that may also contain background, transitions, and related activities, resulting in inexact supervision in the input space ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) . At the class level, candidate pseudolabeling retains several plausible classes from model predictions to generate the candidate label set ( Zhang et al., 2024 ) . It contains the true label and several false-positive labels, which does not specify the true label and provides inexact supervision in the output space ( Wang et al., 2025 ) . Multi-instance partial-label learning (MIPL) captures both forms of inexact supervision by representing each example as a bag of instances paired with a candidate label set containing its true label and several false-positive labels ( Tang et al., 2024c ) . We formulate this setting as video classification with MIPL (VCMIPL) , where each bag is an ordered sequence of frame or clip features and its supervision is a candidate label set.

blocks.en: Existing methods offer several ways to learn from inexact supervision. Attention-based MIPL couples bag representation learning with momentum-based label disambiguation ( Tang et al., 2023 ) . In partial-label learning, prototype-guided disambiguation ( Wang et al., 2022b ; Jin et al., 2025 ) and transport-based label refinement ( Wang et al., 2022a ; Gu et al., 2025 ) exploit feature geometry and assignment constraints, respectively. Weakly-supervised video classification jointly learns classification and temporal instance selection from explicit video-level labels ( Wang et al., 2017 ) . However, in VCMIPL, temporal evidence must be inferred while the true class remains ambiguous. Although instance selection and label disambiguation can interact during learning, refining bag-level class probabilities alone does not determine how temporal evidence is allocated to each candidate class. Distinct class–time assignments can yield identical class probabilities, even when they assign the same total mass to every temporal position. This motivates learning from a structured class–time target that combines refined class beliefs with temporal allocation inferred within the candidate set.

blocks.en: In this paper, we propose a VCMIPL method named PivotMipl , i.e., Plan Inference via Variable-Occupancy Transport for Multi-Instance Partial-Label learning , which represents each video through a class–prototype–time assignment. A temporal encoder produces contextualized features that are matched to multiple prototypes per class on the unit sphere. Temporal occupancy, the mass assigned to each position, is inferred jointly with the assignment, with regularization discouraging excessive concentration. During training, we re-solve the assignment within the candidate label set to obtain a proposal and refine its class marginal through momentum accumulation. A KL projection then constructs the closest teacher to this proposal subject to the refined class marginal and the proposal’s temporal occupancy. A single plan-level KL objective aligns the full-space predictor with the structured teacher. At test time, prediction uses only the full-space assignment, requiring neither candidate labels nor teacher construction.

blocks.en: We construct three VCMIPL benchmarks based on Breakfast ( Kuehne et al., 2014 ) , DoTA ( Yao et al., 2023 ) , and FineAction ( Liu et al., 2022 ) datasets, using four feature representations. Extensive experimental results on the benchmarks show that PivotMipl achieves the highest mean accuracy and balanced accuracy in 10 of 12 configurations, averaging gains of 3.16 % 3.16\% and 3.26 % 3.26\% over the strongest baseline per configuration, respectively. And the accuracy is significantly higher than the strongest baseline in 8 of 12 configurations. Ablations support the contributions of occupancy regularization, adaptive temporal allocation, joint class–time supervision, dual-marginal teacher construction, multiple prototypes, and temporal encoding. Gains persist in 10 configurations against AgopMipl ( Cao et al., 2026 ) , which is the strongest baseline, with the same temporal encoder. Further analyses show favorable accuracy–training-time trade-offs in several configurations and stable performance over the tested regularization ranges on three representative configurations.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are threefold:
First, we introduce a structured framework for VCMIPL that couples candidate-restricted temporal allocation with label disambiguation through a joint assignment and a teacher constrained by class and temporal marginals.
Second, we analyze the inference and supervision mechanisms, characterizing the relationship between candidate re-solving and masking, the concentration control induced by occupancy regularization, and the effective supervision provided by the joint objective.
Third, we construct three VCMIPL benchmarks with model-generated candidate label sets with four feature representations, and evaluate the framework against representative MIPL methods on the benchmarks.

我们的贡献有三:
首先,我们为VCMIPL引入了一个结构化的框架,即夫妇通过联合任务和教师受到班级和时间边际的限制,在限定时间分配上限制候选人,并标出混淆的标签。
第二,我们分析推论和监督机制,描述候选人重新溶解和蒙面之间的关系,通过占用正规化而导致的集中控制,以及共同目标提供的有效监督。
第三,我们构建了三个VCMIPL基准,其模式生成的候选标签集有四个特征说明,并在基准上对照有代表性的MIPL方法评价框架。

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Multi-Instance Partial-Label Learning
blocks.zh: 2.1 多举措部分标签学习

blocks.en:
MIPL learns from bags with ambiguous candidate labels, addressing inexact supervision in both instance and label spaces. Tang et al. (2024c) introduced instance-level probabilistic disambiguation, whereas Tang et al. (2023) used attention-based bag representations and momentum-refined label beliefs. Subsequent methods exploit complementary candidate- and non-candidate-label information ( Tang et al., 2024b ) , attention and prediction margins ( Tang et al., 2024a ) , probabilistic generative modeling of latent label distributions ( Yang et al., 2024 ) , and instance- and bag-level dependencies and heterogeneity for computational efficiency ( Yang et al., 2025 ) .
Recent approaches incorporate candidate-aware propensity scoring and deconfounding ( Luo et al., 2026 ) , feature and label propagation over bag- and instance-level graphs ( Zhu et al., 2026 ) , feature geometry based on average gradient outer products ( Cao et al., 2026 ) , aggregation uncertainty through evidential learning ( Jie et al., 2026 ) , and prediction calibration ( Tang et al., 2026 ) .
However, our focus is on the specific coupling of candidate-restricted temporal occupancy, historical class beliefs, and a teacher constrained by class and temporal marginals.
blocks.zh:
MIPL从带有模棱两可的候选标签的袋子中学习,在实例和标签空间中处理不准确的监督问题。 唐等编. (2024c)引入了实例级概率分解,而Tang等人则引入了. (2023年)使用以关注为主的袋式表示和动力改进后标签信仰. 随后的方法利用互补的候选和非候选标签信息(Tang等,2024b),注意力和预测边距(Tang等,2024a),潜在标签分布的概率基因模型(Yang等,2024),以及计算效率的实例和袋位依赖性和异性(Yang等,2025年)。
最近的办法包括:候选人的倾向分分和分解(Luo等,2026年),在袋和实例图上传播特征和标签(Zhu等,2026年),根据平均梯度外出产物进行几何学分(Cao等,2026年),通过证据学习汇总不确定性(Jie等,2026年)和预测校正(Tang等,2026年)。
然而,我们的重点是具体结合受考生限制的时间占用、历史阶级信仰以及受阶级和时间边际制约的教师。

blocks.en: 2.2 Weakly Supervised Video Learning
blocks.zh: 2.2 弱监督视频学习

blocks.en: Weakly supervised video learning infers temporal evidence from video-level labels. UntrimmedNets represents videos as temporal segments and jointly learns segment selection and video-level classification ( Wang et al., 2017 ) . Later methods model intra- and inter-segment dependencies ( He et al., 2022 ) , organize evidence into proposals ( Ren et al., 2023 ) , and infer salient snippet features from variations between neighboring time steps ( Yun et al., 2024 ) . PseudoFormer progressively converts weak predictions into more reliable pseudo supervision for temporal localization ( Liu and Liu, 2025 ) , while multimodal large language models provide semantic priors ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) . These methods generally assume unambiguous video labels. Our setting additionally requires identifying the true class within a candidate set and linking it to supporting temporal evidence.
blocks.zh: 监督不力的视频学习推断出视频级别标签中的时间证据. UntrimmedNets代表视频作为时间段并共同学习分段选择和视频级别分类(Wang等,2017. 后期方法建模了区内和区间依附关系(He等,2022年),将证据整理成提案(Ren等,2023年),并推断出相邻时间步间变化的突出片段特征(Yun等,2024年). PseudoFormer逐渐将弱预测转换为更可靠的伪监督时间定位(Liu和Liu,2025年),而多式大语言模型则提供语义前传(Zhang等,2025a.). 这些方法一般都带有清晰的视频标签. 我们的设定还需要确定一组候选人中的真正类别,并将其与支持时间证据联系起来。

blocks.en: Table 1 shows that PivotMipl achieves the highest mean ACC in 10 of the 12 dataset–feature configurations, with an average gain of 3.16% over the strongest baseline in each configuration. Beyond the overall improvement, the performance pattern supports the central motivation of our framework. Most competing MIPL methods ultimately resolve ambiguity through bag-level class supervision, without explicitly retaining which temporal evidence supports each candidate class. In contrast, PivotMipl preserves this class–time association throughout disambiguation, so that the plan-level objective constrains both the class belief and its supporting temporal allocation. This distinction is particularly evident with the frame-level DINOv3 and ResNet representations, where PivotMipl consistently ranks first across all three datasets. These representations leave temporal dependencies largely unresolved before MIPL learning, making explicit evidence allocation especially useful for separating informative instances from background or class-irrelevant content. The main exceptions occur in VideoMAEv2, where strong baselines already achieve highly competitive performance. A plausible explanation is that its clip-level representations already encode substantial local spatiotemporal context, reducing the remaining ambiguity that can be resolved by downstream temporal restructuring. Nevertheless, PivotMipl is inferior to AgopMipl in only one configuration while being significantly superior to the strongest competing method in eight, suggesting that its advantage primarily stems from coupling label disambiguation with temporal evidence allocation rather than from a particular feature backbone.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We presented PivotMipl , a structured framework coupling candidate-label disambiguation with temporal evidence allocation for video multi-instance partial-label learning. Occupancy-regularized spherical transport matches contextualized features to multiple prototypes per class, learning nonuniform temporal assignments while discouraging excessive concentration. Candidate-restricted inference and dual-marginal KL projection construct a teacher that integrates momentum-refined class beliefs while preserving the proposal’s temporal occupancy. A single plan-level KL objective aligns the full-space predictor with this teacher. Our analysis characterizes when candidate re-solving differs from masking and establishes, under the proposed construction, the objective’s decomposition into class-marginal alignment and class-conditional temporal supervision. Across Breakfast-MIPL, DoTA-MIPL, and FineAction-MIPL with four feature representations, PivotMipl achieves the highest mean ACC and BACC in 10 of 12 configurations. Ablations support the joint objective and dual-marginal teacher, while encoder-matched comparisons suggest gains beyond temporal encoding. These findings support resolving label ambiguity through explicit class–time associations rather than class probabilities alone.
blocks.zh: PivotMipl是一个结构化的框架, 使用规范的球形运输将背景化的特性与每个班级的多个原型相匹配,学习非统一的时间任务,同时抑制过度集中. 候选人受限制的推论和双重边际KL投射构筑了一个教师,在保持提案的时间占用性的同时,融合了动力改良的阶级信仰. 一个单一的计划级KL目标将全空间预测器与这位老师相配合. 我们的分析描述的是,候选人的再溶解与遮掩不同,并在拟议的结构下确定目标分解为分级-边际调整和分级时间监督。 在整个早餐-MIPL、DOTA-MIPL和Fine Action-MIPL中,共有四个特色表述,PivotMipl在12个配置中的10个组合中实现了最高的中间ACC和BACC. 分解支持了联合目标和双边教师,而编码器相匹配的比较则表明增益超出了时间分解. 这些结论支持通过明确的班级-时间协会,而不仅仅是班级概率来解决标签模糊问题。

We construct VCMIPL benchmarks from Breakfast ( Kuehne et al., 2014 ) , DoTA ( Yao et al., 2023 ) , and FineAction ( Liu et al., 2022 ) . Table 3 summarizes the video counts, class counts, and candidate-set sizes. Each example consists of an ordered video bag and a candidate label set containing its ground-truth class. For FineAction, we retain videos with a single annotated target class and exclude classes containing fewer than 50 videos. The resulting benchmarks contain 1,989 videos from 10 classes for Breakfast, 4,577 videos from 9 classes for DoTA, and 10,675 videos from 78 classes for FineAction.
In the output space, we generate candidate labels using a VideoMAEv2 recognizer equipped with a TimeSformerHead in MMAction2 ( MMAction2 Contributors, 2020 ) . Candidate probabilities are obtained through five-fold cross-fitting: the recognizer is fine-tuned using the exact video labels from four folds and predicts the remaining fold. Repeating this procedure produces an out-of-fold prediction for every video. The recognizer is fine-tuned for 30 epochs on DoTA and 100 epochs on both Breakfast and FineAction.

blocks.en: We adopt a fixed five-fold evaluation protocol for all three benchmarks. In each fold, four predefined folds are used for training and the remaining fold for testing, and the reported ACC and BACC are averaged over the five held-out folds. Candidate labels are generated in an out-of-fold manner using the same fold partition: the candidate recognizer is fine-tuned on four folds and applied to the held-out fold, and this procedure is repeated until every video receives an out-of-fold prediction. The downstream MIPL models are then trained using only the resulting candidate label sets as supervision. PivotMipl is optimized for 40 epochs with one complete video bag per optimization step, without temporal padding, and the same training protocol is used across all feature representations unless otherwise specified. Ablation studies are conducted on Fold 1 and evaluated at epoch 40. Detailed optimization, architecture, transport, and teacher-projection settings are summarized in Table 5 .

blocks.en: Table 6 further confirms the advantage of PivotMipl under class-balanced evaluation. PivotMipl achieves the highest mean BACC, the mean recall over ground-truth classes represented in each test fold, in 10 of the 12 dataset–feature configurations, with an average gain of 3.26% over the strongest baseline. Notably, the improvement pattern closely follows that of ACC, indicating that the gains are not primarily driven by better prediction on dominant classes, but extend across the class distribution. PivotMipl also ranks first in all four DoTA-MIPL configurations, where the substantially lower BACC values make balanced recognition particularly challenging. The only exceptions again occur with VideoMAEv2, suggesting that the reduced headroom observed in the ACC results persists under class-balanced evaluation.

blocks.en: C.3.1 Ablation Summaries
blocks.zh: C.3.1 概述

blocks.en: Table 7 shows that the gains of PivotMipl are distributed across multiple components rather than dominated by a single design choice. Replacing the plan-level objective with class-level KL (A3) or removing the temporal-marginal constraint from the teacher (A4) degrades performance in all 12 configurations, highlighting joint class–time supervision and dual-marginal projection as the most structurally consistent contributors. Removing the temporal encoder (A6) causes the largest average drop, while the strong performance gap retained against encoder-matched baselines indicates that temporal contextualization alone does not explain the full advantage. Finally, A1, A2, and A5 show that occupancy regularization, adaptive temporal allocation, and multiple prototypes each provide complementary gains, supporting the need to model both temporal concentration and intra-class variation.

blocks.en: C.4 Parameter Sensitivity Analysis
blocks.zh: C.4 参数灵敏度分析

blocks.en: We examine the sensitivity of PivotMipl to the two transport-specific hyperparameters, the entropic coefficient ε \varepsilon and the occupancy coefficient λ \lambda in Eq. ( 8 ), using three representative Fold-1 configurations: Breakfast–ResNet, DoTA–VideoMAEv2, and FineAction–SlowFast. As shown in Figure 3 , performance varies only moderately over the evaluated ranges for both parameters, despite substantial differences in dataset scale and feature representation. The two parameters play complementary roles in the transport inference: ε \varepsilon controls the sharpness of the class–prototype–time assignment, whereas λ \lambda regulates the concentration of the temporal marginal. A very small ε \varepsilon favors sharper matching, while increasing it produces smoother assignments; similarly, increasing λ \lambda discourages excessive concentration of mass on a small number of temporal positions. The relatively broad performance plateaus therefore suggest that PivotMipl does not depend on a narrowly tuned balance between these two effects. Instead, the structured teacher and plan-level supervision remain effective under a range of assignment smoothness and temporal occupancy regularization strengths. This robustness is particularly desirable in VCMIPL, where sequence length, temporal redundancy, and feature granularity vary substantially across datasets.

blocks.en: Our study focuses on offline VCMIPL within a fixed label space. Although the experiments span multiple datasets and feature representations, they do not establish robustness to distribution shifts or evolving class vocabularies. Assessing how class–time associations transfer across such changes remains a direction for future work. Moreover, the current formulation uses bidirectional temporal context and normalizes assignments over the observed video. Extending it to strictly online prediction would require causal contextualization and incremental assignment updates that account for incomplete temporal evidence.
